chunks: Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I brought up with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) the matter of what they narrate regarding the sighting [of God]. So he said: The sun is one part of seventy parts of the light of the Footstool (al-Kursi), and the Footstool is one part of seventy parts of the light of the Throne (al-Arsh), and the Throne is one part of seventy parts of the light of the Veil, and the Veil is one part of seventy parts of the light of the Curtain. So if they were truthful, then let them fill their eyes from the sun when there is no cloud beneath it.

key_terms.الحجاب: The Veil (al-Hijab) — a divine barrier or screen beyond the Throne that conceals the divine reality
key_terms.الرؤية: The 'sighting' (ru'ya) — the contested theological question of whether God can be physically seen; this term here refers to the Sunni hadith tradition claiming believers will see God on the Day of Judgment
key_terms.الستر: The Curtain (al-Sitr) — the outermost divine concealment; beyond the Veil, representing the absolute transcendence of the divine light
key_terms.العرش: The Throne (al-Arsh) — the highest cosmic structure in Islamic cosmology, described as encompassing the heavens and earth
key_terms.الكرسي: The Footstool (al-Kursi) — a cosmic entity mentioned in Quran 2:255 (Ayat al-Kursi); in Islamic cosmology, it represents the divine footstool and is subordinate to the Throne

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about the sighting of God and the hierarchy of divine light?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) responds to reports about the physical 'sighting' (ru'ya) of God by presenting a cosmological argument against it. He describes a four-level hierarchy of divine light — Kursi, Arsh, Hijab, Sitr — each being seventy times greater than the previous, showing that the sun itself is a vanishingly small fraction of God's light. The argument is a reductio ad absurdum: if one cannot gaze at the sun unobstructed, how could any creature ever behold the source of all light directly? This aligns with the Shia theological position denying the corporealist interpretation of divine vision.
